title: Best Power Strips 2026: Surge Protectors Ranked by Real Customer Ratings
description: The best-rated power strips and surge protectors on Amazon, ranked by real customer ratings on surge protection, outlet count, and value. Find the right strip for a desk, TV setup, or whole-room use.
quickAnswer: The SUPERDANNY Power Strip with 22 AC outlets and 6 USB ports delivers the most capacity for the price at 4.8 stars — 22 grounded outlets plus USB at about $21. If you want a premium pick, the Anker 12-outlet strip with 2100J surge protection and 20W USB-C charging is the most-loved higher-end option. And for a simple, reliable budget strip, the HANYCONY 1080J braided model is a top-rated bargain.

howWeChose.heading: How We Chose These Strips
howWeChose.intro: We rank products the honest way: by digging through real Amazon customer reviews. Here is our process:
steps: Star-rating analysis: We surface the top-rated power strips in the category and note their real Amazon ratings.

Review reading: We read through hundreds of verified buyer reviews to find which strips hold up — plugs that stay in, surge protections that actually work, USB ports that deliver — and which ones buyers warn against.
Feature matching: We break down the real differences between flat-plug, braided-cord, AC-outlet-count, and USB-charging designs.
Value matching: We rank the best option for desks, media centers, and whole-room surge protection.
howWeChose.closing: Each product's rating below is its real Amazon rating — a reflection of what real buyers reported, not our own hands-on testing.

whoThisIsFor: This guide is for anyone setting up a desk, a home office, a TV stand, or a workshop and wants a power strip that's safe, reliable, and has enough outlets. Whether you need basic outlets or surge protection with USB charging, we've ranked options for every setup and budget.
We focused on power strips with surge protection and enough outlets for typical home and office use, from compact 6-outlet strips to high-capacity 22-outlet models.

grid.p: Just extra outlets, sometimes with a switch. Cheapest, but they offer no surge protection. Fine for low-value devices, but avoid for expensive electronics.
Add surge protection that absorbs voltage spikes from the wall. Essential for protecting TVs, computers, and other expensive electronics. Look for a joule rating (higher = better).
Include USB-A and/or USB-C charging ports so you can charge phones and tablets without a wall adapter. Convenient for desks and nightstands.
The plug lays flat or turns sideways so it doesn't block the other outlet or stick out from the wall. Great for tight spaces behind furniture.

items: Surge protection: Look for a joule rating — 1000J is decent, 2000J+ is good for expensive electronics. Without surge protection, a strip is just extra outlets.
Outlet count: Count what you actually plug in. A desk might need just 6 outlets; a media center or workbench might want 12-22.
USB ports: USB-C is faster for modern phones and laptops. If you need USB at all, prefer a model with at least one USB-C port.
Flat plug vs straight plug: If the strip goes behind furniture, a flat plug stops it from crowding the wall outlet.
Cord length and type: Braided cords resist wear and are more flexible. Longer cords reach farther but remember: don't chain strips together.
Rating density: A high star rating across many thousands of reviews is a stronger signal than a high rating on a handful.

care.heading: Care & Safety
care.intro: Keep your power strip safe and working with these tips:
items: Don't daisy-chain: Never plug one strip into another. It can overload the circuit and cause a fire. Use one properly sized strip.
Don't overload: Stay under the strip's amperage rating. If it gets hot to the touch, you're drawing too much.
Keep it dry: Power strips are indoor gear — keep them away from sinks, spills, and damp areas.
Give it airflow: Don't bury a strip under rugs or pile it with fully covered cables; heat needs to escape.
Replace after a big surge: Surge protectors wear out after absorbing a strong surge. If the protection light is off, replace the strip.
Unplug during storms: A direct lightning strike can overwhelm even a surge protector. Unplug sensitive gear during severe storms when you can.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a power strip and a surge protector?
faqs.a: A basic power strip just adds outlets — it has no surge protection. A surge protector absorbs voltage spikes from the wall to protect attached electronics. If you're plugging in anything expensive (TV, computer), use a surge protector. The protection level is measured in joules; higher is better.

faqs.q: How many outlets do I need on a power strip?
faqs.a: Count what you actually plug in and add a little headroom. A desk typically needs 6-8 outlets; a TV stand or media center often wants 10-20. High-capacity strips like the SUPERDANNY (22 outlets) are for when you're consolidating a lot of devices around one spot.

faqs.q: What does a surge protector's joule rating mean?
faqs.a: Joules measure how much energy a surge protector can absorb before it fails. A 1000J rating protects against small everyday surges; 2000J+ offers better protection for expensive electronics. After a large surge the protector can be spent, often signaled by a status light going off.

faqs.q: Is it safe to plug a power strip into another power strip?
faqs.a: No. Connecting strips together (daisy-chaining) can overload the circuit and cause overheating or fire. If you need more reach, use one longer, properly rated cord. If you need more outlets, use one higher-capacity strip.

faqs.q: Should I get a power strip with USB ports?
faqs.a: USB ports are convenient for a desk or nightstand because they charge phones, tablets, and earbuds without a separate wall adapter. Prefer a model with USB-C for faster charging of modern devices. Just note USB ports don't add surge protection on strip models without a separate rating.
